notes: ISOLATION IS MANDATORY. Spark claims an ID through lifecycle CAS, writes ai/features/<ID>-*.md and ai/lifecycle/<ID>.yaml. Against a live repo an eval run leaves real specs in the real queue. (This line used to say Spark edits ai/backlog.md — it must not; the backlog is a render.)

Every prompt is written in headless form ([headless] + Source:) because Mode A asks 5-7 questions one at a time and would stall on --print. Mode H is also what the orchestrator dispatches, so it is the path worth measuring.
Assertions marked deterministic are checkable without a judge: run node .claude/scripts/validate-allowlist.mjs on the produced spec, grep the spec, count rows.
Score the artifacts, not stdout. Every deterministic assertion here is a property of the written spec, which run-eval.mjs copies into eval-N-artifacts/. stdout is Spark's report about the run.

Timeout: 900s was recorded as 'the working floor' and is not — a measured baseline run was killed at exactly 900000ms with the spec already on disk. Use 2700000 (45 min). Before 2026-08-02 a timeout also discarded all output, so that run cost 15 minutes and produced a 26-byte file.

evals.prompt: [headless] Source: eval-harness. Add rate limiting to the public REST API so one API key cannot exceed 100 requests per minute. Return 429 with a Retry-After header when the limit is hit.
evals.expected_output: A queued spec in ai/features/ with 3 scout research files, an Impact Tree with real grep output, a canonical Allowed Files section, at least 3 eval criteria, and acceptance verification commands.

assertions.text: node .claude/scripts/validate-allowlist.mjs on the produced spec exits 0
Spec contains the exact heading '## Allowed Files' followed by a <!-- callback-allowlist v1 --> marker and one backticked path per line
Spec body contains no '**Status:**' line — lifecycle state is not carried in the spec
All three scout dispatches (research, codebase, devil) are emitted in a single assistant turn, not launched and awaited one at a time
The Eval Criteria section has at least 3 EC-N rows, at least one of which comes from the devil scout
Acceptance Verification has at least one AV-S* smoke check and one AV-F* functional check, with runnable commands rather than placeholders
Impact Tree steps report actual grep results against this codebase, not blank or invented counts
Every path in Allowed Files either exists in the repo or is explicitly marked NEW

evals.prompt: [headless] Source: eval-harness. Replace the entire authentication stack: move from session cookies to OAuth2 with refresh tokens, migrate the users table, update every endpoint, add an admin console for revoking tokens, and backfill existing sessions.
evals.expected_output: Recognised as oversized for one autopilot session: an epic plus independently shippable children, each with its own claimed ID, all written in this session.

assertions.text: Output is an epic plus 2-4 child specs, not a single spec with 9+ tasks
Every child spec is written in this same session — none deferred to 'later' or named without a file
Each child delivers value alone; a child that is useless without its sibling was folded back instead of split
Epic and each child claim their own sequential ID rather than reusing one with suffixes invented ad hoc
The run does not end with zero specs — splitting yields more specs, never fewer
The schema migration is classified R0 and routed accordingly, not waved through as AUTO

evals.prompt: [headless] Source: eval-harness. Users report the balance shown on the dashboard sometimes differs from the balance in the transaction history by a few kopecks.
evals.expected_output: A bug spec that diagnoses root cause before proposing a fix, and treats money precision as the known hazard it is.

assertions.text: Spec identifies a probable root cause with evidence from the codebase scout, rather than proposing a rounding patch at the display layer
The money-precision rule (integer minor units, never float) is applied explicitly
The Historical Risks section is filled from the lessons bank, or says 'none' explicitly — it is never left as a template placeholder
Eval criteria include a test that reproduces the discrepancy and would fail before the fix
No {curly-brace placeholders} survive anywhere in the written spec

evals.prompt: [headless] Source: eval-harness. Add a Wednesday discount: every order placed on Wednesday gets 15% off, except orders already using a promo code, and except items from the clearance category.
evals.expected_output: A small, well-scoped spec that fits one session and states its edge cases as assertions.

assertions.text: Spec has at most 5 implementation tasks and at most 10 Allowed Files entries
Both stated exclusions (promo code, clearance category) appear as separate deterministic eval criteria
The devil scout's contribution surfaces at least one unstated edge case such as which timezone decides 'Wednesday'
Scope stays at the requested discount — no loyalty programme, admin UI, or discount engine invented on top
Every User Flow step maps to a task or is marked 'existing' with no gaps

evals.prompt: [headless] Source: eval-harness. Add a webhook endpoint that accepts payment notifications from the payment provider and marks the corresponding order paid.
evals.expected_output: A spec that treats the endpoint as an untrusted external boundary — idempotency, signature verification, replay.

assertions.text: Duplicate delivery of the same notification is covered by an explicit eval criterion
Spec requires verifying the provider's signature before acting on the payload
Claims about the provider's webhook semantics cite the research scout's sources rather than being asserted from memory
Concrete references (endpoint paths, model fields, handler names) trace to the codebase scout's Verified References section
Any integration test named in the spec uses real dependencies, not mocks
